Team — forwarding Verdant's ask. Quick constraints:
- Primary workload: mostly long-context retrieval + multi-turn summarization. ~5% of requests require 50k–70k tokens, majority < 4k tokens.
- Latency SLO: interactive (95th < 350ms) for short flows; long flows can be async but need bounded completion.
- Target cost: keep monthly inference cost within range in their workbook (see attachment).

My initial thought: recommend mixed pool: L4 for 80% of short interactive load (cheaper, good for lower latency on small contexts), A100 for medium/long contexts where memory and throughput balance matters, and a small H100 reserve for rare 70k-token jobs and batching-heavy offline work. We should define concrete slotting / routing policies and a fallback policy to spin on burst (if they take reserve + burst) or fall back to a quantized A100 variant.

Irene/Prioy: can you run the quick latency-vs-cost sketch from the metrics PDF and confirm the sizing (how many reserved slots of each type to recommend for a 10M monthly token baseline)? Ben — include commercial ask (how to phrase burst/reserve language so procurement accepts it).

-karthik

Maya / Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: mixed pool recommendation + contract language suggestions below. More detail in the attached proposal.

Recommendation summary (one-paragraph):
- Base reserved pool: 6 x A100 (40GB) slots + 12 x L4 slots. This gives predictable medium-context throughput and cheap front-line handling for interactive traffic.
- H100 reserve: 1 x H100 (80GB) for guaranteed headroom on the rare 70k-token jobs and heavy batch/LLM fine-tune jobs; define a canary policy so H100 usage is monitored and only used when necessary.
- Burst allowance: 30% burst capacity across pools for seasonal spikes, billed at pay-as-you-go rates.

Why this split: A100 provides a good balance of memory and throughput for 8k–32k contexts with lower unit cost than H100. L4 is cost-effective for low-memory, latency-sensitive short requests. H100 is overprovisioned for most traffic but required for extreme long-context cases due to memory headroom.

Contract / procurement suggestions:
- Define reserved slots by SKU and host (e.g., ReservedSlot[A100-40GB]=6). Include a clause for cross-SKU fallbacks (e.g., "If reserved SKU unavailable, requests may be routed to compatible SKU with notice"), and a maximum failover frequency.
- For procurement comfort, offer a monthly metering report and a 30-day lookback for burst adjustments; cap burst spend at X% of committed value unless pre-approved.
- SLA parity: SLA should be inventory-agnostic (we guarantee route-level latency SLOs). If customer requires SKU-specific SLAs on H100-backed latency for long-context, that should be a paid add-on.

Next steps: I attached a short proposal PDF and a cost spreadsheet. Karthik — can you confirm the exact numbers from ops? Irene / Priyom — any ops red flags to call out?

Best,
